title: Effective Horndeski Reduction of the EFC Perturbation Sector
description: Shows that, on an FRW background in the quasi-static sub-horizon regime, the linear perturbation equations of Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) admit an effective mapping to the Bellini–Sawicki Horndeski α-function basis. Identifies αT = 0, derives αM ∝ S(a) and αB ∝ dS/d ln a from the EFC dynamics, and isolates a scale-dependent stiffness response R(k, z) with no direct BS analogue that suppresses µ(k) on cosmological scales. This closes the formal gap between the EFC action and Euclid’s EFT/hi_class pipeline for linear perturbations.

efc_action.latex: S_{\rm EFC} = \int d^4x\,\sqrt{-g}\,\Big[\tfrac{1}{2} M_{\rm Pl}^2 F(\phi) R - \tfrac{1}{2} K(\rho) g^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial_\nu\phi - V(\phi) - \lambda\, (\Box\phi - \Gamma(\rho))\Big]
efc_action.description: EFC relativistic action with density-dependent kinetic stiffness K(\rho) and a Lagrange-multiplier flow constraint enforcing \Box\phi = \Gamma(\rho).

background_constraint.description: Background evolution constraint on FRW; fixes \bar\phi via the entropy production rate evaluated on the background density.

subhorizon_delta_phi.description: In the quasi-static sub-horizon regime the scalar perturbation is slaved to the matter perturbation by the flow constraint.

epsilon_parameters.description: Dimensionless control parameters for the EFC perturbation sector on sub-horizon scales.

stiffness_response.description: Scale-dependent stiffness response arising from the density dependence of K(\rho); produces a suppression in \mu(k, z).

observables_eta_mu_sigma.description: Closed-form expressions for gravitational slip \eta, effective Newton coupling \mu, and lensing combination \Sigma at leading order in the quasi-static expansion.

alphaM_definition.latex: \alpha_M \equiv \frac{d\ln M_*^2}{d\ln a}\,,\qquad M_*^2 = M_{\rm Pl}^2 F(\phi)\quad\Rightarrow\quad \alpha_M = \frac{F_{,\phi}}{F}\,\frac{d\phi}{d\ln a}
alphaM_definition.description: Bellini–Sawicki Planck-mass running; for F(\phi)=1+\alpha_\phi\phi this links directly to the background solution for \phi(a).

alphaB_effective.description: Effective braiding induced by the flow-constraint term; peaks where the entropy sigmoid S(a) transitions.

alphaK_effective.description: EFC kineticity sourced by the density-dependent kinetic stiffness and scalar background velocity.

alphaT_zero.description: Tensor speed equals light speed (c_T=c), consistent with GWs; in BS language the tensor sector is standard (no excess).

key_results.main_finding: In the FRW quasi-static sub-horizon limit, EFC linear perturbations map to an effective Bellini–Sawicki representation with αT=0, αM ∝ S(a), and αB ∝ dS/d ln a, while a distinct stiffness response R(k, z) produces scale-dependent µ suppression beyond standard Horndeski.

sealed_predictions.statement: Tensor propagation speed equals the speed of light at late times (αT = 0, c_T = c) in the EFC effective description.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Multi-messenger GW–EM timing constraints (e.g., binary neutron star mergers) at z < 1 detecting |c_T/c − 1| > 10^-15.

sealed_predictions.statement: The effective braiding parameter peaks during the entropy-flow transition, with αB(z) tracking dS/d ln a (single-peaked around the transition scale factor).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Tomographic LSS and lensing analyses constraining the time profile of αB(z), e.g., Euclid/LSST EFT fits inconsistent with a single-peaked derivative-of-sigmoid profile.

sealed_predictions.statement: On linear sub-horizon scales, µ(k, z) shows a scale-dependent suppression below unity at cosmological k that relaxes to GR (µ → 1) toward galactic/solar scales due to R(k, z) → 0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Joint RSD–weak lensing–CMB lensing constraints on µ(k, z) detecting no suppression or an opposite trend (µ ≥ 1 with no k-dependence) across 0.01 < k < 1 h Mpc^-1.

kill_criteria: KC1: Detection of a non-luminal tensor speed at low redshift (|c_T/c − 1| > 10^-15) implying αT ≠ 0, inconsistent with the EFC effective tensor sector.

KC2: Tomographic reconstructions of αM(z) that are inconsistent at >3σ with a monotonic sigmoid-like evolution S(a) driven by the background flow constraint (e.g., multiple disjoint transitions or opposite overall sign).

KC3: Joint RSD and lensing constraints showing µ(k, z) ≥ 1 with no significant scale dependence (or increasing with k) across 0.01 < k < 0.5 h Mpc^-1 at >3σ, contradicting the predicted R(k, z)-induced suppression and µ → 1 at high k.
KC4: High-density and Solar-System tests detecting |µ − 1| > 10^-5 where R(k, z) → 0 should recover GR, indicating failure of the EFC stiffness-screening behavior.

KC5: Numerical pipeline validation fails: the mapped BS α-functions cannot reproduce EFC linear observables {η(k, z), µ(k, z), Σ(k, z)} within 1% over 0 < z < 2 and 0.01 < k < 1 h Mpc^-1 in the quasi-static regime.

related_packages.role: Foundational EFC action and perturbation framework referenced as Ref. [1].
